drhp.expansion: The Company completed its brownfield expansion project at the existing plant location in December 2025, taking installed cement production capacity to 4 Million Tons per annum. Separately, the Company is pursuing statutory approvals for two limestone mining leases — the Rata Mandha-1A (RM-1A) Block in Jaisalmer District, Rajasthan (preferred bidder since December 2021, LOI issued March 2023, subject to a pending Rajasthan High Court writ petition) and the Block II - Saidulnama Block in Suryapet District, Telangana (170.74 hectares; preferred bidder since November 2024, LOI issued January 2025) — to secure future limestone supply.

litigation.note: The Company has challenged, in the High Court of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, a District Mineral Foundation contribution demand raised by Singareni Collieries Company Limited (its coal supplier under a Fuel Supply Agreement) relating to coal mining royalty; the matter remains pending.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- CRISIL expects Indian cement demand to grow around 6.5-7.5% in FY27, primarily from infrastructure and industrial/commercial construction.
- The South Indian cement industry has a positive demand outlook, but margins remain under pressure in the near term because of capacity additions and intense competition.
- South India — particularly Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka — is likely to remain one of India's most important cement markets, driven by infrastructure projects (highways/expressways, irrigation, ports, metro/urban infrastructure, industrial corridors, airports, power projects, data centres, warehousing/logistics, railways).
- Excess production facilities in a region may lead to tougher competition; the cement industry is highly dependent on construction activity.
- Scarcity in supply of raw material, and increases in power, fuel, steel and other building-material costs, are cited as threats to consumption and margins.
- The current-quarter outlook is not encouraging, but the outlook for the future is expected to be stable, supported by ongoing and proposed infrastructure projects.

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: The Company completed its brownfield expansion project at the existing plant location in December 2025, taking installed cement production capacity to 4 Million Tons per annum. Separately, the Company is pursuing statutory approvals for two limestone mining leases — the Rata Mandha-1A (RM-1A) Block in Jaisalmer District, Rajasthan (preferred bidder since December 2021, LOI issued March 2023, subject to a pending Rajasthan High Court writ petition) and the Block II - Saidulnama Block in Suryapet District, Telangana (170.74 hectares; preferred bidder since November 2024, LOI issued January 2025) — to secure future limestone supply.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- cost position: waste heat recovery and captive power reduce energy costs — evidence: Waste Heat Recovery Power Plant for Kiln & Cooler exit gasses, Captive Power Plant generating Bottom Ash and Fly Ash used in PPC manufacturing
- distribution: dedicated rail-based logistics for both inbound coal and outbound cement — evidence: Railway siding for Cement Loading at Plant and wagon tippler facility for coal unloading
- resource (reserve life): preferred bidder for two limestone mining leases to extend raw-material supply [planned] — evidence: declared preferred bidder for RM-1A Block (Rajasthan) in Dec 2021 and for Saidulnama Block (Suryapet, Telangana) in Nov 2024 — against it: RM-1A auction remains subject to a pending Rajasthan High Court writ petition and statutory approvals for both blocks are still in process

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Company-flagged risk applicable to the cement business given demand-supply conditions.
- Pricing pressure from additional industry capacity and intense competition in South India could compress margins.
- Rising input costs can erode margins if not passed through in realisations.
- Coal is a key fuel input; supply disruption or price escalation directly affects production costs.
- Higher crude prices raise transportation costs for both input materials and finished goods.
- Policy changes can affect costs, demand and supply for the cement business.
- Capacity additions by competitors in South India intensify competition and pressure pricing.
- The cement industry is heavily reliant on construction activity; any slowdown in construction affects the industry to a large extent.

strategy.body:
- Positioning the Company, following completion of its brownfield expansion, to cater to growing infrastructure development projects in South India.
- Pursuing statutory approvals for two limestone mining leases (Rajasthan and Telangana) to secure long-term raw-material supply.

themes.title: Cement demand & pricing recovery
themes.need: Q1FY27 turned cement from a pricing story into a volume-share-plus-fuel-cost story. ULTRACEMCO grew domestic grey volume +13.1% YoY against an estimated ~7-8% industry, delivered its first Rs 5,000cr+ April-June EBITDA (Rs 5,146cr) with EBITDA/ton held above Rs 1,200, and crossed 200.1 MT domestic capacity a year early - but guided Q2FY27 cost UP ~Rs 130-140/ton and pinned the Rs 1,400/ton consolidated target to Q4FY28. The fuel shock, not price, is the swing factor: JKCEMENT's EBITDA/ton fell to Rs 982 from Rs 1,229 YoY despite +19% grey volume, DALBHARAT flagged pet coke 'surged to nearly $160/t' versus a pre-war $110-115, and NUVOCO defended INR 1,079/ton EBITDA only by cutting petcoke from 37% to 27% of fuel mix in a single quarter. Consolidation is visibly compounding (INDIACEM EBITDA/ton Rs 386->400->509->603 across four quarters; DALBHARAT closed Jaypee at Rs 2,850cr EV with Chunar operational and Rewa on trial within 50 days) even as DALBHARAT slipped its 75mt milestone from FY27 to FY28. SHREECEM/RAMCOCEM/JKLAKSHMI/JSWCEMENT/STARCEMENT/BIRLACORPN ride the same volume + consolidation axis.
themes.driver: Q2FY27 is the guided cost trough - ULTRACEMCO ~Rs 130-140/ton, JKCEMENT ~Rs 150/ton and BIRLACORPN Rs 70-80/ton of incremental cost; then fuel-mix agility (NUVOCO's petcoke swing) and whether DALBHARAT's ~Rs 150/t of procurement savings is really 'permanent, not timing'.
